headline: Margin gains lift earnings despite a soft freight market
summary_short: C.H. Robinson's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 19.3% y/y to $4.93 billion, with diluted EPS up 23.8% to $1.56 and income from operations up 18.4% to $255.7 million even as the freight market stayed in a cyclical trough.
summary_long: Revenue rose 19.3% y/y to $4.93 billion on higher pricing across truckload, LTL, air, and ocean. Adjusted gross profit grew 6.5% to $738.0 million against a 1.0% rise in operating expenses, so income from operations increased 18.4% to $255.7 million and adjusted operating margin expanded 360bp to 34.7%. NAST volume grew 1.5% y/y, the 13th straight quarter of outgrowth versus the Cass Freight Index, while Global Forwarding posted a 33.4% adjusted margin excluding restructuring. Net income rose 22.5% to $186.8 million and diluted EPS rose 23.8% to $1.56. Operating cash flow fell to $35.9 million on a working-capital swing; the company returned $301.3 million to shareholders and guided FY2026 capex to $65-75 million and a tax rate of 18-20%.

drivers.explanation: Higher pricing across truckload, LTL, air, and ocean services drove the increase, with NAST volume up 1.5% y/y, outpacing the Cass Freight Index for a 13th straight quarter.
Adjusted gross profit grew faster than operating expenses (+6.5% vs +1.0%), expanding adjusted operating margin 360bp to 34.7% despite higher incentive compensation and claims costs.
Growth reflects the operating-income increase, partly offset by a slightly higher effective tax rate (21.5% vs 21.4%) and modestly higher net interest and other expense.
EPS growth outpaced net-income growth because diluted weighted-average share count fell 1.1% y/y, reflecting share repurchases over the trailing twelve months.
Debt rose after $1.952 billion of new long-term borrowings during the six months, proceeds used in part to fund $432.2 million of share repurchases and an acquisition.
Not stated directly, but the decline is consistent with $432.2 million of YTD share buybacks and $154.3 million of dividends outweighing YTD net income of $334.0 million.

Management said it hit mid-cycle operating-margin targets in both NAST and Global Forwarding despite the freight market still being in a cyclical trough, crediting market-share gains, disciplined revenue management, and Lean AI productivity gains.
